subject.title: [Bug]:  [Windows] exec spawn: all commands hang with no output (stdio pipe deadlock)

question: Should maintainers spend native Windows/Testbox time now to reproduce this all-command exec hang, or wait for stronger reporter proof before changing process code?
rationale: The source path is plausible and user impact is high, but current main only has mocked Windows coverage and adjacent hardening, not proof of this newer native Windows no-output timeout symptom.

options.title: Run native Windows repro
options.body: Use a native Windows 11 Node 24 setup with a PowerShell-started gateway to capture stdout, stderr, PID, exit status, timeout behavior, and process tree for `echo hello` and `node -v`.

options.title: Wait for reporter evidence
options.body: Keep this issue open but ask for a screen recording, redacted logs, and exact command transcript before maintainer-owned Windows proof is scheduled.

options.title: Defer to adjacent issues only
options.body: Leave the issue open but route only narrower proven fixes such as status timeout or close-fallback timer work until this all-command hang is independently reproduced.

recommendation.title: Run native Windows repro
recommendation.body: Use a native Windows 11 Node 24 setup with a PowerShell-started gateway to capture stdout, stderr, PID, exit status, timeout behavior, and process tree for `echo hello` and `node -v`.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent process-helper and Windows command-spawn history makes this the best available routing owner for deciding proof sufficiency.
